gold: Juvenile spring eruption (JSE) associated with parvovirus B19 infection

selector.rationale: The presence of target lesions, helical thickening, and numerous small blisters, along with the detection of PVB19 DNA in lesional skin biopsy specimen, supports Erythema multiforme as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Phototoxic reaction
rejected.why: The patient had no history of photosensitivity and denied the use of any topical or systemic photosensitizers, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Parvovirus B19 infection
rejected.why: While PVB19 DNA was detected in lesional skin biopsy specimen, the clinical presentation is more consistent with Erythema multiforme, which can be triggered by PVB19 infection.

rejected.label: Gianotti-Crosti syndrome
rejected.why: Although Gianotti-Crosti syndrome is a possible diagnosis, the presence of target lesions and the detection of PVB19 DNA in lesional skin biopsy specimen make Erythema multiforme a more specific and evidence-supported diagnosis.
